newsitem.title: MEXICO: Carroll Foods to put $110 mln into Mexico hog farm.
newsitem.headline: Carroll Foods to put $110 mln into Mexico hog farm.

text.p: U.S. pork producer and turkey importer, Carroll Foods will invest $110 million in a hog farm in the eastern Mexican state of Veracruz, company officials said Friday.
"The investment is under the name Granjas Carroll de Mexico, based in the Valle de Perote, and expects to total $110 million," North Carolina-based company vice-president Pedro Tavares said.

In a meeting with Mexican president Ernesto Zedillo, Tavares said the company's investment will be used to construct 12 hog feedlots, for a total capacity of 30,000 pork bellies and an annual 600,000 hogs for national supply.
The company will later consider the possibility of exporting the product to countries such as Japan, he added.
Tavares said the company's two farms currently supply 2,500 pork bellies each, "allowing us to supply the domestic market with a production of 100,000 hogs per year."

He said the firm is also beginning to construct a cocoa processing plant, which would be built in the Veracruz Industrial Park. The $2 million plant will have an initial annual capacity of 6,000 tonnes, he said.
